To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

an insertion mutation in the rpoD operon makes the sporulation-specific sigma-H gene essential for growth and that the growth defect of this double mutant can be explained by increased expression of genes normally under the control of the major vegetative sigma factor sigma-A.

the insertion of the transposon into orf23 in the csh201::Tn917 mutation causes an increase in the expression of genes under the control sigma-H and that the increase in expression of these genes causes a growth defect in the csh204::Tn917 spo0H double mutation.

the csh203 insertion mutation causes a 2-10-fold increase in sigma-H-dependent gene expression and that the increase in sigma-H expression is responsible for the growth defect of spo0H csh203 double mutants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the expression of the sigma-A gene in Bacillus subtitlis.
the regulation of gene expression in Bacillus subti lis, specifically with the control of the major vegetative sigma factor, sigma A, by the minor vegetative sigma factor sigma H.
the characterization of a mutation that causes an increase in expression of genes controlled in part by sigma-H.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a mutation in the rpoD operon that causes increased transcription of genes controlled by the sigma-H factor makes spo0H an essential gene for vegetative growth.
a mutation in orf23, which is the first gene of rpoD, causes an increase in sigma-H activity, and the increase in sigma-H causes an increase in expression of rpoD and dnaG.

the chs203 mutation causes a decrease in the expression of genes controlled primarily by RNA polymerase holoenzyme containing sigma-A and an increase in the expression of those controlled by sigma-H, and the growth defect of csh203 spoOH is due to a decrease in the level of expression of sigma-A and not to an increase in the level of sigma-H. The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of rpoD is controlled in a complex manner by sigma-H and sigma-A and that the csh203 insertion mutation affects the balance of expression of sigma-A and sigma-H.
the expression of the major sigma factor gene rpoD in B. subtilis is regulated by the sporulation sigma-H.
sigma-H is not essential for vegetative growth, but it is required for optimal growth under normal laboratory conditions.
